tagline: Once around Wheeler Peak, out of Taos and back again.
intro: From Taos the circle goes north on NM 522 to Arroyo Hondo, which grew out of an 1815 Spanish land grant, and on to Questa, then turns east on NM 38 up the old mining valley of the Red River. Over Bobcat Pass, the highest pass in New Mexico, it drops into the Moreno Valley and comes back west on US 64, entering Taos by Kit Carson Road.
All the way round it keeps Wheeler Peak, at 13,161 feet the tallest mountain in the state, in the middle.

moments.title: Red River
moments.text: A gold, silver and copper camp of some 3,000 people in 1895 that got by on trout fishing and cool summers once the ore gave out, and now counts about 540.

moments.title: Eagle Nest
moments.text: The Cimarron River was dammed here in 1918 into a lake at 8,300 feet, over ground where a railroad had bored a tunnel in 1907 for a line to Taos it never finished.

moments.title: Vietnam Veterans Memorial
moments.text: Near US 64 at Angel Fire, at the south end of the Moreno Valley, stands a chapel dedicated in 1971, the first major memorial to the veterans of the Vietnam War.
